abstract.para: Cluster resources automatically fail over (move) to another node during software or hardware failures. However, you can also choose to manually move a resource, either to a specific node or just away from the current node. A move constraint is a location constraint used specifically for moving a resource. The cluster creates the move constraint automatically when you move a resource with &crmsh; or &hawk;.

topic.para: The type of move constraint depends on where you move the resource:

listitem.para: If you move the resource to a specific node, the cluster creates a location constraint with an INFINITY score for the destination node.
If you move the resource away from the current node, the cluster creates a location constraint with a -INFINITY score for the current node.

topic.para: To allow the resource to move back to the original node, you must remove the move constraint. When you remove the constraint, the resource might move back to the original node automatically or it might stay on the destination node, depending on the resource's stickiness.

note.title: Moving a resource vs live migration
note.para: Usually when the cluster moves a resource, it stops the resource on the current node and starts it on the destination node. This is not the same thing as live migration, where the cluster moves a resource from one node to another without stopping it. Live migration is only supported for certain resources and must be enabled for each individual resource.
